prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity desktop personal website mockup for Aaron Cassar, rendered edge-to-edge at a 1440 by 1000 landscape viewport, no browser frame or device. The brief is radically bare bones, incredibly polished, coder-like and simple. This concept is a small calling card floating in enormous quiet cool-white negative space. One small left-aligned composition near the center, with real readable IBM Plex Mono-like typography: 'Aaron Cassar' as modest heading, 'Software engineer.' as secondary text. After generous breathing room: 'I like making things.' and a short smaller line 'Useful ones. Weird ones. Things that work.' A compact row of text links 'work' 'about' 'say hello ↗'. Below the card, a tiny carefully drawn terminal prompt button '>_' with understated label 'there’s more here.' Footer at the viewport lower edges: 'GitHub ↗   LinkedIn ↗   Résumé ↗' on left and 'press ` to explore' on right. Tiny theme toggle upper right, absolutely no top navigation or logo. Cool white #f7f8fa and blue-black ink #242934; one muted steel text shade. No gradients, illustrations, photographs, textures, decorative lines, cards, shadows, status dots, big marketing type or colored accents. Precision, optical alignment, readable typography and emptiness are the whole design. It should look like a beautifully typeset tiny personal note, not a SaaS website. Make the terminal affordance small but discoverable, hinting at a secret command-line interface that opens when clicked.
